the_signal.headline: Chain-of-thought prompting is your agent reasoning tax—optimize it or bleed tokens
the_signal.body: As multi-agent systems scale, CoT prompt overhead becomes a real cost driver, not a nice-to-have. n8n's breakdown shows teams are still using one-size-fits-all reasoning when selective CoT (branching only on high-uncertainty calls) cuts token spend by 30–40%. Your sales automation agent doesn't need to "think aloud" on every lead score—that's cost, not intelligence.

tool_drop.name: OzBrain
tool_drop.what: Shared knowledge layer between AI agents and team members that persists and grows with agent deployments.
tool_drop.why: If your GTM agents are siloed—each one learning separately—you're rebuilding context on every call; OzBrain's agent-first memory model directly addresses why event-driven agent scaling fails without knowledge sync.

thread_of_day.title: Agent-first chat interfaces will replace dashboards—but knowledge portability is the blocker
thread_of_day.takeaway: GTM teams are moving away from dashboard sprawl toward agent-as-interface, but without persistent, shareable knowledge layers, each agent rediscovers the same customer context.

quote.text: RPA versus workflow automation? See how they stack up across reliability, security, scalability, observability, and long-term operations.

whats_moving.context: As GTM agents talk to 5+ vendor APIs, token rotation and key expiry handling become critical—static keys break in production, but most teams still hardcode them.
Token economics just shifted; CoT-heavy agents that were margin-negative might now pencil out, but only if you re-optimize your prompt strategy.
Teams are hitting scaling walls by treating agent orchestration like monoliths—n8n's breakdown on queue vs. stream tradeoffs directly applies to multi-agent sales systems.

act_on_this: Audit your top 3 agent workflows for unnecessary chain-of-thought calls; run A/B tests on selective reasoning (CoT only on low-confidence branches) and measure token savings—you'll likely find 25–35% cost reduction within a week.

numbers.stat: Chain-of-thought reasoning can reduce token efficiency by 3–5x vs. selective reasoning on high-uncertainty calls only
numbers.context: At scale, this compounds—a lead-scoring agent running 10k inferences/day with full CoT burns 5–10M tokens daily; selective CoT drops it to 1.5–2M.
